label: early copy-phase steps whose input is one of x,3,o,l,c,z,r,f,s,d
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase (never during original tokens, essentially never on the delimiter step). Most likely on the first few copy steps (recall_idx 1-3 hold ~90% of the mass; recall_idx 1 alone holds 42%), with a small rise again on the last copy steps of long sequences. Within the copy phase it is gated by the identity of the fed-back input token: x, 3, o, l are strongest (rates 13-22%), then c, z, r, f, s, d; tokens like i and t rarely activate it. The top activations are copy steps 1-2 whose input is x, o, 3 or l. Phase 2 alone has recall ~1.0 but precision 0.12. Adding recall_idx<=3 and the token set gives dev F1 0.50 (P 0.41, R 0.63, mass recall 0.72). Many early-copy steps with favored tokens still do not fire, so the token and position effects are graded, not a clean rule.
